verdict: These are the same caret — same #00B5FF, same 3 CSS px width, same full-line-box height — so this comes down to two pixels of air, and A has them. states.name: caret
states.gap: Caret is 72px tall over a 37px ink band (ascender-to-descender) — a 1.95× overreach versus A's 72/39 = 1.85× — so it towers 19px above the ascenders and 16px below the descenders. It spans exactly 100% of the 72px line pitch: a full-leading block bar filling the entire line box, which reads as a code editor's row marker rather than an instrument sitting in the text.
states.gapTheirs: Caret sits furthest from the actual insertion point: the monospace cell boundary after 'steps' is x=1898 (23px advance, 's' ink ends 1892), and A's caret occupies 1900–1905 — centre 1902.5, i.e. 4.5px right of the boundary versus B's 3.5px. In practice that leaves 7px of dead air between the 's' and the bar and 15px to the following 't'; the caret floats in the gap instead of standing on the character you just typed.
states.verdict: These are the same caret twice, and one pixel decides it: a 6px (≈3 CSS px at 2×) hard-edged cyan slab, #00B5FF at full saturation on a #F9F9F9 ground, with zero antialiasing on any of its four edges, no rounded cap, and no subpixel positioning — a compiler's caret, not a pen. Neither is optically centred on the line: both overhang 3px more above the ascenders than below the descenders (A 18/15, B 19/16), so the bar hangs high in every line you type. B wins only because its caret lands at cell-start+1 instead of A's cell-start+2, so it stays attached to the letter you just typed rather than drifting into the space after it. No selection is rendered in either shot, so half of this dimension is simply untestable — and on a 3px unantialiased bar at 1.9× line-height, that is not a caret a writer would call alive.

states.gapTheirs: An opaque status bar with a 1px #DFDFDF rule at y=1748 is painted over the text column with no bottom padding reserved: the last line's ink is clipped from 37px to 7px. Park the caret there and 65 of its 72px are guillotined — 90% of the instrument gone. A's field runs full-bleed to y=1800 with its final lines intact at full 37px.
states.verdict: These are the same caret — 3px wide, 36px tall, #AFE5FB, hard-edged, identically seated in the line — so anyone claiming a craft difference in the mark itself is inventing one. The only thing that separates them is that B lets a word-count bar chew the bottom of the writing field: type your way down the page in B and the caret gets sliced at the ankles, which is exactly when a writer needs to see it. A wins by not having furniture in the way, not by having a better caret. Both share the real sin: a pale-blue slab at roughly 1.25:1 against #F9F9F9 that vanishes the moment you look away from it.
